candidate.claim: Nominal LLM judge-panel size can substantially overstate independent evidence because judge errors are correlated.

primary_source.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
primary_source.author: Guneet Kohli

MNLI_panel.design: 9 frontier LLM judges from 7 model families on 1,000 ChaosNLI-MNLI items
MNLI_panel.all_nine_wrong: 51/1000 (5.1%), versus <1 expected under the paper's independence model

scaling.interpretation: strong diminishing returns under this measured correlation structure

RewardBench.scope: pairwise preference evaluation with the default MT-Bench-style RewardBench judge prompt; binary pairwise task

chain_of_thought.clarification: In this experiment CoT increased correlation relative to the baseline; this is not a universal claim that CoT always increases judge correlation.

family_diversity.same_vs_cross_family: MNLI same-family correlation exceeds cross-family mean by only 0.047; the three highest-correlated pairs reported are cross-family
family_diversity.one_per_family_panel: 7 judges selecting the best in each family gives n_eff=1.93
family_diversity.clarification: Family diversity alone did not recover independence in this panel; this does not show that all cross-family panels are similarly correlated.

aggregation.headline_scope: established aggregation methods do not close most of the independence/Condorcet gap; on SNLI, AlphaNLI and RewardBench the best individual judge outperforms the listed aggregation methods

scope_clarifications: The paper studies NLI classification and RewardBench pairwise preference judgment, not open-ended program/scientific-hypothesis ranking or O's exact evaluator stack.

n_eff is a correlation-derived effective panel-size diagnostic under the paper's estimation framework; it is not literally the number of independent model calls nor a universal fixed property of a model family.
The paper's n_eff/k < 0.5 warning threshold is diagnostic/heuristic, not an experimentally established universal collapse threshold for evolutionary selection.

The best-single-vs-panel result does not imply a practitioner can identify the best single judge without labels; the paper notes that selecting the best individual also requires oracle/gold information in this comparison.

The transferable evidence is that correlated errors can sharply reduce marginal information from additional LLM judges and can make majority aggregation worse than a strong individual judge in the tested tasks.
confidence: high for paper-reported values and scope; no independent rerun of judge outputs performed
unresolved: Direct measurement of judge-error correlation/effective independence on O-specific open-ended evaluation decisions.
Whether tool-grounded, execution-grounded, or otherwise heterogeneous evidence channels decorrelate errors more effectively than adding model-family diversity.
How n_eff/error correlation causally maps to selection regret or false archive replacement in evolutionary agent search.
downstream_instruction: Retain as strong evidence that nominal judge count is not independent evidence. Do not convert n_eff≈2 for this panel into a universal constant or reject multi-judge evaluation as a family; prefer measuring correlation/effective independence on the target decision distribution.
